One-Week Vegetarian Meal Plan

Balanced, mostly whole-food vegetarian meals with batch-cooking built in. Serves 2 adults. Breakfast and lunch are kept simple so dinners can be the focus.

Recipes

Nutrition values are estimates per serving, calculated from typical ingredient databases. Actual values vary by brand and portion size.

Recipe 1: Chickpea & Spinach Coconut Curry

Serves 4 · Prep 15 min · Cook 25 min · Used Tuesday dinner and Wednesday lunch

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil or coconut oil
  • 1 large yellow onion, finely diced
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
  • 2 tsp curry powder
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 tsp garam masala
  • 1/2 tsp ground turmeric
  • 1 can (400 g) chopped tomatoes
  • 2 cans (400 g each) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
  • 1 can (400 ml) light coconut milk
  • 200 g (about 7 oz) baby spinach
  • 1 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste
  • 1 tbsp fresh lime juice
  • Fresh cilantro, to garnish
  • 1 1/2 cups (about 300 g) dry basmati rice, cooked, to serve

Method

  1. Cook the rice according to package directions and keep warm.
  2. Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden at the edges.
  3. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
  4. Stir in the curry powder, cumin, garam masala and turmeric. Toast for 30 seconds until the spices smell rich.
  5. Pour in the chopped tomatoes, scraping up any browned bits from the pan. Simmer for 5 minutes.
  6. Add the chickpeas, coconut milk and salt. Stir well, reduce heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered for 12 to 15 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.
  7. Fold in the spinach in two batches, stirring until wilted, about 2 minutes.
  8. Remove from heat, stir in the lime juice and taste for salt. Garnish with cilantro and serve over the rice.

Cooking Tips

Toast the ground spices in the oil for a short time before adding liquids. This wakes up their flavour far more than adding them to the sauce raw.
Add a squeeze of lime at the end, not at the start. Acid added early can make the coconut milk taste flat.
To make the curry sweeter and richer, add a diced sweet potato with the tomatoes and extend the simmer by 10 minutes.
Store leftovers in an airtight container for up to 4 days. The sauce thickens in the fridge, so add a splash of water when reheating.

Recipe 2: Mushroom & Lentil Bolognese

Serves 4 · Prep 15 min · Cook 45 min · Used Monday dinner and Tuesday lunch

Ingredients

  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 medium onion, finely diced
  • 2 medium carrots, finely diced
  • 2 celery stalks, finely diced
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 500 g (about 1 lb) cremini mushrooms, finely chopped
  • 1 cup (200 g) brown or green lentils, rinsed
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste
  • 1 tsp dried oregano
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) red wine (optional; use extra broth if omitted)
  • 1 can (800 g) crushed tomatoes
  • 2 cups (480 ml) low-sodium vegetable broth
  • 1 tbsp soy sauce
  • Salt and black pepper, to taste
  • 340 g (12 oz) whole-wheat spaghetti or pasta of choice
  • 1/4 cup (25 g) grated Parmesan (check it is vegetarian-rennet)
  • Small handful of fresh basil, torn

Method

  1. Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 8 minutes, stirring often, until softened.
  2. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
  3. Increase the heat to medium-high, add the mushrooms and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until they release their liquid and it evaporates, leaving them browned.
  4. Stir in the tomato paste and oregano and cook for 2 minutes, until the paste darkens slightly.
  5. Pour in the red wine, if using, and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes until reduced by about half.
  6. Add the lentils, crushed tomatoes, broth and soy sauce. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cover partly and cook for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and the sauce is thick. Add a splash of water if it becomes too dry.
  7. Season with salt and pepper.
  8. While the sauce simmers, cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup of pasta water before draining.
  9. Toss the pasta with the sauce, adding pasta water a little at a time to loosen. Serve topped with Parmesan and basil.

Cooking Tips

Chop the mushrooms very finely, or pulse them in a food processor. Their texture then blends into the sauce and works as a stand-in for minced meat.
Do not rush the mushrooms. Let the moisture fully evaporate before adding the tomato paste; this gives a deep, savoury, "meaty" flavour.
Cook the lentils in the sauce only until tender. Green or brown lentils hold their shape best; red lentils will turn to mush.
The sauce freezes well for up to 3 months. Portion it into freezer bags flat for quick thawing.

Recipe 3: Crispy Tofu & Broccoli Stir-Fry

Serves 2 · Prep 20 min (plus 15 min pressing) · Cook 20 min · Used Wednesday dinner

Ingredients

Tofu and stir-fry

  • 400 g (14 oz) extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into 1-inch cubes
  • 2 tbsp cornstarch
  • 2 tbsp neutral oil (such as avocado or canola), divided
  • 300 g (about 10 oz) broccoli florets, cut into small pieces
  • 1 red bell pepper, sliced into strips
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated
  • 3 green onions, sliced (whites and greens separated)
  • 1 tsp dried red chili flakes (optional)

Sauce

  • 3 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
  • 1 tbsp rice vinegar
  • 1 tbsp maple syrup
  • 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
  • 1 tsp cornstarch

To serve

  • 3/4 cup (about 150 g) dry brown rice, cooked
  • 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds

Method

  1. Cook the brown rice according to package directions.
  2. Wrap the tofu in a clean towel, place a heavy pan on top, and press for 15 minutes to remove excess water. Pat dry.
  3. Toss the tofu cubes with the 2 tbsp cornstarch in a bowl until evenly coated.
  4. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large non-stick skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the tofu in a single layer and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp on all sides. Transfer to a plate.
  5. Whisk together all sauce ingredients in a small bowl so the cornstarch is fully dissolved.
  6. Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the pan. Stir-fry the broccoli and red pepper for 4 to 5 minutes, adding 2 tbsp of water and covering for the last 2 minutes to steam the broccoli until bright green and just tender.
  7. Add the garlic, ginger, white parts of the green onions and chili flakes. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
  8. Stir the sauce again, pour it into the pan and bring to a simmer. Cook for 1 minute until glossy and thickened.
  9. Return the tofu to the pan and toss to coat. Remove from heat, garnish with green onion greens and sesame seeds, and serve over the rice.

Cooking Tips

Press the tofu well. Removing water is what allows the cornstarch coating to crisp rather than steam.
Do not move the tofu cubes for the first 3 minutes of frying. Letting them sit undisturbed builds a crust that releases easily.
Add the sauce only at the end, and keep the heat moderate. Cooking the sauce too long can make the coating soggy.
Cook the tofu in batches if your pan is crowded. Overcrowding drops the temperature and prevents crisping.
